title: Handling Executive Feature Mandates vs High Technical Debt
context: The VP of Sales demands an unannounced custom enterprise feature for an upcoming deal. Simultaneously, the Tech Lead warns that the payment engine will crash if legacy database refactoring is delayed another sprint.
dilemma: How do you balance short-term revenue generation against system stability and technical debt?

must_include: Allocating tech debt capacity budget (e.g., 20% rule)
common_pitfalls: Yielding completely to Sales and ignoring tech debt
Refusing Sales demand outright without compromise

star_model_answer.situation: VP of Sales demanded an urgent feature while Tech Lead flagged severe payment gateway database degradation.
star_model_answer.task: As PO, I had to negotiate a backlog allocation that satisfied commercial deadlines without risking production downtime.
star_model_answer.action: I calculated the Cost of Delay using WSJF. I worked with the team to slice the requested sales feature into a lightweight MVP for contract signing, while dedicating 30% of sprint capacity to essential DB migration.
star_model_answer.result: The sales deal closed successfully with the MVP feature, and the database refactoring prevented a projected 99.9% downtime breach.

title: Splitting a Complex Multi-Month AI Workflow into Deliverable Increments
context: The business requests an automated document processing feature using LLMs. The initial epic estimation is 40 story points, spans 4 sprints, and cannot be tested until all components are finished.
dilemma: How do you split this complex AI story into small, valuable, testable user stories with explicit Given/When/Then acceptance criteria?

must_include: Thin horizontal slice (e.g. mock pipeline -> standard extract -> fallback)
common_pitfalls: Splitting vertically by architectural layers (DB story, UI story, API story)

star_model_answer.situation: An AI document parsing epic was estimated at 40 points and blocked for 4 sprints.
star_model_answer.task: Decompose the epic into thin, testable user stories adhering to BDD and INVEST principles.
star_model_answer.action: Using the SPIDR splitting method, I broke the epic into 4 thin vertical slices: Story 1 (Static PDF extract + manual verify), Story 2 (LLM parser for standard invoices), Story 3 (Confidence score threshold & fallback UI). Drafted clear Given/When/Then criteria for each.
star_model_answer.result: The team delivered working value in Sprint 1, gathering early user feedback and reducing overall epic risk.
